docs.title: Motor
docs.text:
Table 1: Motor Component Selection

Solution Pros Cons Option 1942-PPN7PA12C1-ND$4.50/eachLink to Product * The product is relatively cheap compared to others. * Meets the requirements for the overall design objective of a lampshade. * It is simple to wire. * Requires an external mounting system for the overall project. * Requires a clamping system for the attachment on the shaft of the motor itself. Option 2942-PAN14EE12AA1-ND$6.27/eachLink to Product * The product is not that expensive compared to other ones on the market. * Meets the requirements for the overall design objective of a lampshade that moves up and down to cover a plant. * It is relatively simple to wire. * Also requires an external mounting system for the overall project in order to function. * Requires a clamping system for the attachment on the shaft of the motor itself in order to work. Option 31528-2589-ND$2.95/eachLink to Product * The product is very cheap compared to other ones on the market. * Meets the requirements for the overall design objective of a lampshade that moves up and down to cover a plant. * It is very simple to wire. * This motor also requires an external mounting system for the overall project in order to function. * Requires a clamping system for the attachment on the shaft of the motor itself in order to work. * The shaft is offset by 90 degrees which could very well cause trouble.

Choice: Option 1: 942-PPN7PA12C1-ND DC motor

Rationale: This DC Motor design is where the shaft just comes out straight from the motor instead of having that 90 degree offset like in option 3. As to why I went with this one over option 2, it is because it is cheaper.

docs.title: Solenoid
docs.text:
Table 2: Solenoid Component Selection

Solution Pros Cons Option 11568-11015-ND$6.50/eachLink to Product * The product is pretty cheap compared to other ones on the market. * It meets the requirements for the overall design objective of a valve that switches the flow of water between banks. * It is very simple to wire. * This solenoid requires an external mounting system for the overall project in order to function. * Requires an extension system for the attachment on the shaft of the solenoid in order to connect. Option 21528-2797-ND$7.50/eachLink to Product * The product is pretty inexpensive compared to other ones on the market. * It meets the requirements for the overall design objective of a valve that switches the flow of water between banks. * It is very simple to wire. * This solenoid requires an external mounting system for the overall project in order to function. * Requires an extension system for the attachment on the shaft of the solenoid in order to connect. Option 31144-1402-ND$16.92/eachLink to Product * The product is still slightly cheaper compared to other ones on the market. * It meets the requirements for the overall design objective of a valve that switches the flow of water between banks. * It is not extremely difficult to wire. * This solenoid requires an external mounting system for the overall project in order to function. * It will require a more advanced mounting system.* Requires an extension system for the attachment on the shaft of the solenoid in order to connect.

Choice: Option 1: 1568-11015-ND 5 volts DC solenoid

Rationale: This solenoid design is a push solenoid and it is rated for 5 volts which is what the PIC powers. I like it better than option 2 because the shaft looks easier to connect a water valve ring to. As to why I went with this one over option 3, it is because it is way cheaper and more simple to work with.
